q: About _____ of the mass of the Earth's crust consists of oxygen.
e: About 50% of the mass of the Earth's crust consists of oxygen. 50% is the idea that completes this fact. 21% would fill a different blank than 50%.

q: The free element of oxygen accounts for _____ of the volume of the atmosphere.
e: The free element of oxygen accounts for 21% of the volume of the atmosphere. Free oxygen gas makes up about 21 percent of dry air by volume. 50% would fill a different blank than 21%.

q: In the laboratory, oxygen gas can be prepared by using an environmentally friendly liquid _____ of appropriate strength.
e: In the laboratory, oxygen gas can be prepared by using an environmentally friendly liquid hydrogen peroxide of appropriate strength. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Water would fill a different blank than hydrogen peroxide.

q: In the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide, _____ is used as a catalyst to speed up the chemical reaction.
e: In the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide, manganese(IV) oxide is used as a catalyst to speed up the chemical reaction. Manganese(IV) oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Potassium chlorate would fill a different blank than manganese(IV) oxide.

q: Oxygen gas is collected by the _____ of water.
e: Oxygen gas is collected by the downward displacement of water. Downward displacement is the idea that completes this fact. Downward delivery would fill a different blank than downward displacement.

q: The chemical equation for the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide is _____.
e: The chemical equation for the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide is 2H2O2(aq) MnO2 2H2O(l) + O2(g). 2H2O2(aq) MnO2 2H2O(l) + O2(g) is the idea that completes this fact. H2O2(aq) MnO2 H2O(l) + O2(g) would fill a different blank than 2H2O2(aq) MnO2 2H2O(l) + O2(g).

q: Oxygen is a colourless gas, without taste or smell, and is only _____ soluble in water.
e: Oxygen is a colourless gas, without taste or smell, and is only slightly soluble in water. Slightly is the idea that completes this fact. Completely would fill a different blank than slightly.

q: Oxygen will not burn, however, it _____ combustion.
e: Oxygen will not burn, however, it supports combustion. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal. Prevents is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Oxygen rekindles any glowing thing (splinter) with a _____.
e: Oxygen rekindles any glowing thing (splinter) with a bright flame. Bright flame is the idea that completes this fact. Dazzling white flame would fill a different blank than bright flame.

q: When magnesium burns in oxygen from air, it leaves a white powder residue which is _____.
e: When magnesium burns in oxygen from air, it leaves a white powder residue which is magnesium oxide. Magnesium oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Magnesium hydroxide would fill a different blank than magnesium oxide.

q: The chemical equation for the burning of magnesium ribbon in oxygen is _____.
e: The chemical equation for the burning of magnesium ribbon in oxygen is 2Mg(s) + O2(g) 2MgO(s). 2Mg(s) + O2(g) 2MgO(s) is the idea that completes this fact. 2Mg(s) + O2(g) Mg2O(s) would fill a different blank than 2Mg(s) + O2(g) 2MgO(s).

q: Iron slowly becomes oxidised in the presence of air and water to form hydrated iron(III) oxide, which is commonly known as _____.
e: Iron slowly becomes oxidised in the presence of air and water to form hydrated iron(III) oxide, which is commonly known as rust. Rust is the idea that completes this fact. Bauxite would fill a different blank than rust.

q: Non-metals such as phosphorus, sulphur and carbon react with oxygen forming _____.
e: Non-metals such as phosphorus, sulphur and carbon react with oxygen forming oxides. Oxides is the idea that completes this fact. Chlorides would fill a different blank than oxides.

q: Red phosphorus burns in oxygen giving off white fumes which consist of _____.
e: Red phosphorus burns in oxygen giving off white fumes which consist of oxides of phosphorus. Oxides of phosphorus is the idea that completes this fact. Phosphorus hydride would fill a different blank than oxides of phosphorus.

q: An acidic oxide is an oxide of _____.
e: An acidic oxide is an oxide of non-metal. Acidic oxides are usually non-metal oxides that make acids with water or react with bases. Metalloid would fill a different blank than non-metal.

q: An acidic oxide reacts with basic oxides to give _____ only.
e: An acidic oxide reacts with basic oxides to give salts only. Basic oxides are usually metal oxides that react with acids to make salt and water. Salts and water would fill a different blank than salts.

q: Acidic oxides react with alkali solutions to give _____.
e: Acidic oxides react with alkali solutions to give salts and water. Salts and water is the idea that completes this fact. Salts and hydrogen would fill a different blank than salts and water.

q: The test for carbon dioxide involves passing it into calcium hydroxide solution, which turns milky due to the formation of _____.
e: The test for carbon dioxide involves passing it into calcium hydroxide solution, which turns milky due to the formation of calcium carbonate. Calcium carbonate is the idea that completes this fact. Calcium bicarbonate would fill a different blank than calcium carbonate.

q: Among the following, the insoluble acidic oxide is _____.
e: Among the following, the insoluble acidic oxide is SiO2. SiO2 is the idea that completes this fact. CO2 would fill a different blank than SiO2.

q: Soluble acidic oxides dissolve in water to form acidic solutions. These solutions turn blue litmus _____.
e: Soluble acidic oxides dissolve in water to form acidic solutions. These solutions turn blue litmus red. Red is the idea that completes this fact. Blue would fill a different blank than red.

q: A basic oxide is an oxide of _____.
e: A basic oxide is an oxide of metal. Metal is the idea that completes this fact. Non-metal would fill a different blank than metal.

q: A basic oxide reacts with an acid to produce _____.
e: A basic oxide reacts with an acid to produce a salt and water only. A salt and water only is the idea that completes this fact. An acid and water only would fill a different blank than a salt and water only.

q: Among the following, the insoluble basic oxide is _____.
e: Among the following, the insoluble basic oxide is MgO. MgO is the idea that completes this fact. K2O would fill a different blank than MgO.

q: Some basic oxides react with water forming hydroxide solutions (alkalis). These solutions turn red litmus _____.
e: Some basic oxides react with water forming hydroxide solutions (alkalis). These solutions turn red litmus blue. Blue is the idea that completes this fact. Red would fill a different blank than blue.

q: An amphoteric oxide is a metallic oxide which possesses _____.
e: An amphoteric oxide is a metallic oxide which possesses both basic and acidic properties. A property is physical if measuring it leaves the substance itself unchanged, and chemical if composition changes. Only acidic properties would fill a different blank than both basic and acidic properties.

q: An amphoteric oxide reacts with both acids and alkalis to form _____.
e: An amphoteric oxide reacts with both acids and alkalis to form salt and water. Salt and water is the idea that completes this fact. Salt and hydrogen would fill a different blank than salt and water.

q: Which of the following is an example of an amphoteric oxide?
e: ZnO is an example of an amphoteric oxide. An amphoteric oxide, such as ZnO, can react with both acids and bases. CO2 is not an example of an amphoteric oxide.

q: A neutral oxide is an oxide which shows _____.
e: A neutral oxide is an oxide which shows neither basic nor acidic character. Neither basic nor acidic character is the idea that completes this fact. Both basic and acidic character would fill a different blank than neither basic nor acidic character.

q: Which of the following is an example of a neutral oxide?
e: CO is an example of a neutral oxide. A neutral oxide such as CO or N2O does not form an acid or a base with water. CO2 is not an example of a neutral oxide.

q: Peroxides are oxides that react with an acid to give salt and _____.
e: Peroxides are oxides that react with an acid to give salt and hydrogen peroxide. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Hydrogen gas would fill a different blank than hydrogen peroxide.

q: Which of the following is an example of a peroxide?
e: BaO2 is an example of a peroxide. A peroxide contains an O-O link, as in H2O2 or BaO2. MnO2 is not an example of a peroxide.

q: $PbO_2$, $MnO_2$ and $NO_2$ are not peroxides because they _____.
a: do not give hydrogen peroxides on reaction with acids
e: PbO2, MnO2 and NO2 are not peroxides because they do not give hydrogen peroxides on reaction with acids. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Do not react with acids is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: A compound oxide is an oxide, formed by the combination of two different oxides of the _____.
e: A compound oxide is an oxide, formed by the combination of two different oxides of the same element. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom. Same compound would fill a different blank than same element.

q: Which of the following is an example of a compound oxide?
e: Pb3O4 is an example of a compound oxide. A compound oxide behaves as if two oxides are combined, like Pb3O4. MgO is not an example of a compound oxide.

q: $Pb_3O_4$ can be written as di-lead(II) lead(IV) oxide or _____.
e: Pb3O4 can be written as di-lead(II) lead(IV) oxide or red lead oxide. Red lead oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Black lead oxide would fill a different blank than red lead oxide.

q: When red lead oxide reacts with dilute nitric acid, only _____ reacts with the acid to form lead(II) nitrate.
e: When red lead oxide reacts with dilute nitric acid, only lead(II) oxide reacts with the acid to form lead(II) nitrate. Lead(II) oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Lead(IV) oxide would fill a different blank than lead(II) oxide.

q: In living organisms, the oxygen intake is used for the breakdown of the _____ molecules to produce energy.
e: In living organisms, the oxygen intake is used for the breakdown of the glucose molecules to produce energy. Glucose is the idea that completes this fact. Protein would fill a different blank than glucose.

q: Liquid oxygen is carried on rockets to _____.
e: Liquid oxygen is carried on rockets to support the fuel burns. A fuel is a substance that releases useful energy as it changes chemically, usually by burning. Cool the engine would fill a different blank than support the fuel burns.

q: Which oxide is used in fire extinguishers?
e: CO2 is oxide is used in fire extinguishers. CO2 is the idea that completes this fact. MgO is a different claim from CO2.

q: Which oxide is used as a bleaching agent?
e: SO2 is oxide is used as a bleaching agent. SO2 is the idea that completes this fact. CO2 is a different claim from SO2.
